master.title: UPDATE: RUSSIA-UKRAINE CONFLICT, May 12 as of 16:00 (Msk)
master.content:
Putin accuses West of provoking global crisis by pursuing anti-Russian sanctions

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Russia is confidently handling external economic challenges amid the sanction policy pursued by Western states, which would face negative implications that would be hard to reverse, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"The sanctions [by Western states] are actually what's provoking a global crisis. Their authors, guided by nearsighted excessive political ambitions and Russophobia, are rather dealing a blow to their own national interests, their own economies, and the wellbeing of their own citizens," Putin said at a conference on economic affairs on Thursday.

This is evident in particular from an inflation spike in Europe, as consumer prices in the Eurozone on the whole have risen by over 11%, and some countries are seeing yearly inflation reach nearly 20%, Putin said.

"It's obvious that, due to objective economic laws, the continuation of the sanction mania will inevitably lead to dramatic and hardly reversible implications for the EU, for its citizens, as well as for the poorest countries, which are already facing risks of starvation. I'd stress that the responsibility for this fully and completely rests with the Western elites, which are ready to sacrifice the rest of the world for the sake of preserving their global dominance," Putin said.

"Russia, for its part, is confidently handling external challenges, owing both to a responsible economic policy of the past years and systemic solutions bolstering its economic sovereignty and technological and food security," he said.

Russian companies are gradually occupying the niches vacated on the domestic market by some "unscrupulous partners," including as regards the production of everyday necessities, industrial and service equipment, construction and agricultural machinery, and others, he said.

Putin: Russia's grain harvest could total 130 mln tonnes in 2022, including record 87 mln tonnes of wheat

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Russia's grain harvest could total 130 million tonnes in 2022, including a record 87 million tonnes of wheat, according to preliminary data, President Vladimir Putin said at a government meeting on Thursday.

"A good harvest is expected this year. According to the experts, and these are of course preliminary estimates, the grain harvest could total 130 million tonnes, including 87 million tonnes of wheat. If this does happen, and we are counting specifically on this, then it [the wheat harvest] would be an all-time record in Russia's entire history," Putin said.

"This would not only allow meeting domestic needs, with plenty to spare, it would also allow increasing supplies to the global market for our partners, which is very important for worldwide foodstuffs markets," the president stressed.

Russia harvested an all-time high of 135.5 million tonnes of overall grain crops in 2017, with the wheat harvest totaling 86 million tonnes.

The country harvested 133.5 million tonnes of grain in 2020, including 85.9 million tonnes of wheat, though the grain harvest declined to 121.4 million tonnes in 2021, including 76 million tonnes of wheat.

Key difficulties for Russian economy remain: logistics chains disrupted, imports have fallen - minister

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - The Russian economy is showing a resilience with no sharp drop in output or growth in unemployment, but key difficulties like disrupted logistics chains, a drop in imports and need for working capital at companies, remain, Economic Development Minister Maxim Reshetnikov said at a meeting between President Vladimir Putin and cabinet ministers.

"The Russian economy is indeed demonstrating resilience amid unprecedented sanctions pressure. The currency and financial markets situation has stabilized. There has been no sharp decline in production or considerable growth in unemployment. A shortage of goods has been averted and the wave of panic demand has subsided. Inflation has slowed substantially," Reshetnikov said.

"But key difficulties do of course remain. Logistics chains are disrupted and production needs to be reconfigured, and companies are still very much in need of working capital. And issues with employment and personal incomes are always high on the agenda," he said.

Everyone wants to avoid direct clash between Russia, NATO - Peskov

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Both Moscow, Brussels and, most importantly, Washington want to avoid a direct military confrontation between Russia and NATO, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

"Everyone, including Russia, wants to avoid a direct clash between Russia and NATO. Such statements have been repeatedly made by NATO and, most importantly, by Washington, including at the highest level. President Biden has also made such statements," Peskov said at a press briefing on Thursday in response to a question whether the probability of a direct conflict between Moscow and the alliance was increasing amid the Ukraine situation.

The Kremlin relies on statements by Russian President Vladimir Putin that "Russia will be ready to give the most resolute response to the side that tries to somehow 'interfere' in Ukraine and the special military operation that is being conducted by the Russian Armed Forces in Ukraine," he said.

No attempts at resuming Russia-U.S. dialogue made over past 2 months - Peskov

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - There have been no attempts at resuming Russia-U.S. dialogue over the past two months, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

Journalists asked Peskov at a press briefing on Thursday whether the U.S. had tried to arrange bilateral talks at the summit level since the beginning of the special operation in Ukraine. "As you remember, President Putin and the Russian side have been trying to avoid the special military operation before it began. Yet they did not want to talk and to listen to us," Peskov said.

"There have been no attempts at resuming the dialogue over the past two months," he said.

Security of Russian regions bordering Ukraine needs to tighten over attacks - Peskov

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - The attack on the Belgorod region requires the provision of stronger security of districts bordering Ukraine, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

The attack on the Belgorod region from Ukraine, in which a Russian civilian died, was mentioned at Peskov's press briefing on Thursday. Journalists asked Peskov whether the incident might have an effect on the provision of security in Russian regions bordering Ukraine.

"This situation requires additional measures to enhance the security of districts bordering Ukraine," Peskov said.

The Russian military will speak about specific measures, he said.

Journalists also asked how the incident might affect the prospects of Russian-Ukrainian talks.

"We talked about the negotiations yesterday. Nothing has changed since then. We have nothing to boast of on the negotiating track," Peskov said.

Finland's accession to NATO to pose threat to Russia - Peskov

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Finland's accession to NATO will pose a threat to Russia, Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov said.

"Of course, it will," Peskov told reporters in response to the relevant question.

"Another enlargement of NATO does not make our continent more stable and secure," he said.

Russia to analyze consequences of Finland's accession to NATO for national security - Peskov

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Russia will make a special analysis upon Finland's accession to NATO to elaborate measures for the provision of national security, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

"As you remember, there is an order from the president, the supreme commander-in-chief that a list of measures be composed to strengthen our western flanks in connection with the strengthening of the eastern flank of NATO. NATO has been enlarging towards us. So, clearly, all of that will be elements of a special analysis and the elaboration of measures necessary for maintaining a balance and providing our security," Peskov told reporters in response to a question on how Russia could respond to Finland's accession to NATO.

"Everything will depend on the manifestation of the further [NATO] enlargement process, how far the military infrastructure will grow towards our borders," Peskov said.

Russia to give military-technical, other responses to Finland's possible accession to NATO - Foreign Ministry

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Russia will give military-technical and other responses to Finland's possible accession to NATO, the Russian Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Thursday.

"Finland's accession to NATO will do serious harm to the bilateral Russian-Finnish relations and the provision of stability and security in Northern Europe. Russia will have to take military-technical and other countermeasures to mitigate the threats to its national security emerging in that connection," the ministry said.

Russia "has repeatedly noted that the choice of ways to ensure national security was up to the authorities and the people of Finland. At the same time, Helsinki should be aware of the responsibility and consequences of such a move," the ministry said.

The Russian Foreign Ministry also believes that "accession to NATO will be a direct breach of international legal obligations of Finland, above all, the Paris Peace Treaty of 1947, by which the sides pledge not to form unions or join coalitions targeting either of them, as well as the 1992 Treaty on Foundations of Relations between Russia and Finland, which says that the sides will not use force or threaten to use force against each other's territorial integrity or political independence, and will not use or allow to use their territory for an armed aggression against each other," it said.

"However, given the current disregard for international law by the collective West, this kind of behavior has become normal. We will respond depending on the situation," the ministry said.

"The policy of military non-alignment has been a foundation of stability in Northern Europe, has been providing a solid security level for the Finnish state, and has served as a pillar of mutually advantageous cooperation and partnership between our states, in which the role of the military factor has reduced to zero, for decades," it said.

"Neither Russia's assurances of the absence of any hostile intentions in regard to Finland nor the long history of neighborly, mutually advantageous cooperation between our countries have persuaded Helsinki of the advantage of continuing the policy of military non-alignment," the ministry said.

The ministry believes that "the goal of NATO, whose members have been fiercely convincing the Finnish side of the lack of an alternative to its membership in the alliance, is clear, i.e. to carry on the enlargement towards Russia and to create yet another flank for military threat to our country." "But why would Finland turn its territory into a line of military confrontation with the Russian Federation, thus losing the ability to make independent decisions, is for history to judge," it said.

Russian Foreign Ministry protests against 'illegal commercial activity' at Dutch consulate general in St. Petersburg

MOSCOW. May 12 (Interfax) - Russia has protested to the Dutch charge d'affaires ad interim in connection with the illegal commercial activity conducted on the premises of the Dutch consulate general in St. Petersburg, the Russian Foreign Ministry said in a statement on its website.

"Dutch Charge d'Affaires ad interim to Russia Martijn Elgersma was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry on May 12, and a strong protest was voiced in connection with the illegal commercial activity conducted on the premises of the consulate general of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in St. Petersburg," the ministry said.

Elgersma was told about "the inadmissibility of using consulate grounds for purposes incompatible with consular duties and the need for all-inclusive measures to prevent violations of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations of 1963," the ministry said.

Troops training on Belarusian border during surprise check of response forces - top security official

MINSK. May 12 (Interfax) - Servicemen are conducting combat training near the state border of Belarus as part of the surprise inspection of the country's response forces, Belarusian Security Council Secretary Alexander Volfovich said.

"Our border service divisions monitor and see everything, and not only divisions of the border service, but our reconnaissance military units, i.e. electronic reconnaissance and radio reconnaissance units, see it as well. We see all this both in the west and in the south: all relocations of groups of, let's say, neighboring states. Naturally, we have to react to this situation. Mindful of it, the Defense Ministry, the defense minister adopted a decision to hold a surprise check of the response forces. It is based on the combat training plans," Volfovich told the STV channel.

This decision was approved and reported to the head of state, he said.

"The president of the country endorsed it. And, in order to practice combat training plans and combat training missions, we sent response forces to areas unfamiliar to them. We sent them not only to training ranges, but also to areas in the vicinity of the state border - both the southern border and the western border," Volfovich said.

The Belarusian Defense Ministry said earlier that Volfovich visited Belarusian battalion tactical groups intended to reinforce the state border. During the trip, he assessed the units' potential to tackle combat tasks and the moral and psychological state of their personnel and familiarized himself with the organization of measures to maintain weapons and military and specialized hardware and servicemen's off-duty life.

Ukraine decides to seize Ukrainian assets of Russia's Sberbank, VEB

KYIV. May 12 (Interfax) - Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council has decided to seize assets in the country belonging to Russia and its residents, such as 99.8% of shares in Prominvestbank (PIB) owned by Russian development corporation VEB.RF and 100% of shares in International Reserve Bank owned by Sberbank.

The Council decision of May 11, which was confirmed the same day by a decree issued by Ukraine's president, also calls for the seizure of financial assets in the form of VEB.RF's rights to PIB debt totaling UAH0.93 billion and Sberbank's rights to International Reserve Bank debt totaling UAH14.9 billion.

Ukraine is also seizing other financial assets of these subsidiaries of Russian banks, with the exception of UAH3 billion belonging to International Reserve Bank that will be used to meet claims from creditors.

The council decision and presidential decree were published on the website of Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada on Thursday.

According to published documents, the seizure does not apply to the rights under loans from International Reserve Bank to rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia with about $166 million debt outstanding, to Electrotyazhmash - UAH516.9 million, Artyom holding company - UAH205.1 million and Zorya-Mashproekt - UAH2.325 billion, as well as for the rights under a PIB loan to Ukrzaliznytsia for $231.6 million, which are subject to transfer [probably to National Investment Fund, which the government designated for this role on May 10].

According to the National Security and Defense Council's decision, the Cabinet of Ministers and the Deposit Guarantee Fund, together with the National Bank, must ensure that these assets of the Russian Federation and its residents are seized within 10 days of the date of the decree's publication.

The Verkhovna Rada on Thursday approved a presidential decree of May 11 on the seizure of the Ukrainian assets of Sberbank and VEB.RF.

VEB said on Thursday that issues related to the expropriation of assets and compensation of losses will be resolved in international arbitration. It said the Stockholm tribunal recognized VEB as "an independent investor, and not a government body or part of the state."

Sberbank plans to challenge the seizure by Ukraine of its assets in that country. "Sberbank is initiating investment arbitration against Ukraine with a claim for damages based on the agreement of November 27, 1998 between the government of the Russian Federation and the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine on the encouragement and mutual protection of investments," the Russian bank said in a statement.

The Ukrainian government on April 9 decided to expropriate the corporate rights and financial assets removed from the market by International Reserve Bank and Prominvestbank. The decision is essentially the practical implementation of the Law on the Expropriation in Ukraine of Assets of the RF and its Residents, the Cabinet of Ministers said.

"Ukraine is recovering part of its financial assets in the form of claims on debt, funds in accounts, government bonds and [NBU] certificates of deposit [NBU]. So of course, the next decision should be a decision by the National Security and Defense Council, but this important step [towards expropriation] has already been made today," First Deputy Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko said at the time.

The National Bank of Ukraine in March 11 sent a letter to the Cabinet of Ministers, in which it proposed to seize the financial assets of International Reserve Bank and Prominvestbank. The NBU envisaged that the state might receive around UAH 26 billion.

Both banks had their licenses withdrawn in February.
